source_metadata.title: SKILL-USE: Can LLMs Actually Use Skills in Agentic Harnesses?
source_metadata.source_type: arXiv preprint / AI agent benchmark paper

atoms.canonical_statement: The study aimed to evaluate whether LLM agents can autonomously recognize, retrieve, and correctly apply relevant skills under progressive disclosure.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We introduce SKILL-USE, a benchmark that evaluates skill use under progressive disclosure.

atoms.canonical_statement: The benchmark decomposed skill use into Trigger, Compliance, and Boundary, corresponding to skill retrieval, procedural adherence, and avoidance of prohibited operations.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: SKILL-USE separates three facets of skill use. Trigger measures whether the agent invokes the relevant skill, Compliance measures how faithfully it follows the prescribed procedure, and Boundary measures whether it avoids forbidden operations.

atoms.canonical_statement: The Skill-Use score gated execution credit on successful retrieval of the target skill.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: SU(y) = g(y; s) [α C(y) + (1 − α) B(y)]

atoms.canonical_statement: The Skill-Use score used a compliance weight α of 0.7 and a boundary weight of 0.3.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We fix α = 0.7 throughout the paper, giving Compliance the larger weight.

atoms.canonical_statement: Each evaluation instance consisted of a skill, a user task, an executable sandbox, and a hidden scoring rubric.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: An instance is a tuple x = (s, q, E, R) containing a skill s, a user task q, an executable sandbox E, and a scoring rubric R.

atoms.canonical_statement: Agents initially received only the task, sandbox, and skill metadata; the full skill procedure was withheld until the agent retrieved the skill file.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The agent initially receives (q, E, m) as input. It does not receive p.

atoms.canonical_statement: Trigger was defined as a binary indicator of whether the target skill was retrieved in the execution trajectory.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Trigger is g(y; s) := I[Retrieve(s) ∈ τ].

atoms.canonical_statement: Compliance was defined as the weighted proportion of prescribed skill requirements satisfied.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Compliance is C(y) := ...

outcome.definition: Weighted fraction of prescribed requirements satisfied

atoms.canonical_statement: Boundary was defined as the weighted proportion of prohibited behaviors that were absent.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Boundary is B(y) := ...

atoms.canonical_statement: SKILL-USE contained 79 real skill entries paired with 177 executable tasks across nine domains.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: SKILL-USE contains 79 real skill entries paired with 177 executable tasks across nine domains.

atoms.canonical_statement: The benchmark included 1,314 rubric items, averaging 7.4 items per rubric and ranging from 3 to 16.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The 177 rubrics hold 1,314 scoring items, averaging 7.4 per rubric and ranging from 3 to 16.

atoms.canonical_statement: Tasks contained an average of 4.8 skill-exclusive requirements, with a maximum of 12.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: each task carries 4.8 such requirements on average, with a tail reaching 12.

atoms.canonical_statement: Skills were retained only when they contained requirements not inferable from the task request or generic practice.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Skill exclusivity. The skill must contain requirements that cannot be inferred from the task request or generic practice.

atoms.canonical_statement: Skills were retained only when their procedures constrained observable agent behavior in trajectories or artifacts.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Process observability. The skill must constrain how the agent acts and leave verifiable evidence in its trajectory or artifacts.

atoms.canonical_statement: The construction pipeline used masked-skill screening to remove requirements that strong models could satisfy from the task prompt and generic practice alone.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The masked-skill check drops any requirement a strong model still meets from the prompt alone.

atoms.canonical_statement: Task and rubric artifacts underwent cross-family multi-agent adversarial review before release.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: A cross-family adversarial review then requires reviewers from different model families to confirm each such requirement.

atoms.canonical_statement: Rubric items were organized into evaluability gates, skill-derived Compliance and Boundary items, and task-outcome items excluded from the Skill-Use score.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Evaluability gates determine whether the run can be scored, skill-derived items measure Compliance and Boundary, and task-outcome items record whether the requested result was produced.

atoms.canonical_statement: Deterministic verifiers were preferred, with a scope-restricted LLM judge used only when a requirement could not be reliably expressed as a rule.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We prefer deterministic checks and use a scope-restricted LLM judge only when a requirement cannot be expressed reliably as a rule.

atoms.canonical_statement: Every skill-task-rubric triple was validated for executability, cross-component consistency, and rubric reliability.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: retain only instances that satisfy three criteria: Executability... Cross-component consistency... Rubric reliability.

atoms.canonical_statement: The skill-selection funnel narrowed approximately 105,586 public GitHub skill candidates to 79 released skills.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Four phases narrow 105,586 public GitHub skills to 79.

atoms.canonical_statement: Rule scoring required separate thresholds of at least 0.30 for constraint density and 0.25 for style specificity.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: τden = 0.30 and τsty = 0.25.

atoms.canonical_statement: Tier A skills required at least three exclusive constraints, at least two rule-verifiable constraints, and coverage of at least two dimensions.
Eight LLMs from seven model families were evaluated under Claude Code and Codex harnesses.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We evaluate eight LLMs from seven families... Each model is evaluated under two agent harnesses, Claude Code (CC) and Codex.

atoms.canonical_statement: Each benchmark task ran in an isolated Docker sandbox.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Every task runs in an isolated Docker sandbox.

atoms.canonical_statement: LLM-judge rubric items were scored by GPT-5.4 at temperature 0.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Rubric items judged by an LLM use GPT-5.4 at temperature 0.

atoms.canonical_statement: Model sampling used temperature 0, top-p 1.0, and high reasoning effort where available.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We sample at temperature 0, top-p 1.0, and reasoning effort “high” where offered.

atoms.canonical_statement: Gemini-family models were excluded because a gateway schema sanitizer made the Skill tool non-invokable.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We exclude the Gemini family from every analysis: its channel runs a schema sanitiser that renames or drops fields in the Skill tool.

atoms.canonical_statement: The turn limit was 120 under Claude Code and 80 under Codex, with a 1,500-second wall-clock limit.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The turn limit is 120 under CC and 80 under Codex... the wall-clock limit is 1,500s.

atoms.canonical_statement: Approximately 2.8% of raw traces failed trace checks and were rerun.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: About 2.8% of raw traces fail and are re-run.

quantitative_result.original_result_text: About 2.8% of raw traces failed and were rerun

atoms.canonical_statement: The highest observed Skill-Use score was 0.613 for GPT-5.5 under Claude Code.
Under Codex, Claude Opus 4.8 had the highest Skill-Use score at 0.559.

quantitative_result.original_result_text: Claude Opus 4.8 under Codex achieved SU 0.559

atoms.canonical_statement: The highest conditional Compliance among triggered traces was 0.638.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Even among triggered traces, the highest Compliance† reaches only 0.638.

quantitative_result.original_result_text: Highest Compliance on triggered traces was 0.638

atoms.canonical_statement: Boundary scores exceeded Compliance scores for every model-harness configuration in the main results.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Boundary is higher than Compliance across all model-harness configurations.

atoms.canonical_statement: Triggering and procedural compliance behaved as distinct bottlenecks: some models rarely selected a skill despite reasonable conditional compliance, while others triggered often but executed poorly.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Triggering and procedural compliance break down as separate bottlenecks.

atoms.canonical_statement: Skill-use scores and model rankings changed across harnesses, indicating that performance was a property of the model-harness configuration rather than the model alone.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: SU is therefore a property of a model-harness configuration, and rankings under one harness may not transfer to another.

atoms.canonical_statement: GPT-5.5 conditional Compliance decreased by more than 0.1 when moving from Claude Code to Codex.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: with GPT-5.5’s Compliance† falling by more than a tenth.

concept.text: Harness change from Claude Code to Codex

atoms.canonical_statement: File processing, database, and data science skills had the highest category-level Compliance, while business analysis and software architecture scored lower.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: File processing, database, and data science skills have the highest Compliance... Business analysis and software architecture score lower.

atoms.canonical_statement: Security and compliance was the only category where Compliance exceeded Boundary.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Boundary exceeds Compliance in every category except Security & Compliance.

atoms.canonical_statement: The skill-injection experiment paired native progressive-disclosure runs with runs in which the complete skill document was preloaded into the initial instructions.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: In the native mode... the model must actively open the file... In the preloaded mode, the entire skill document is inserted into the initial instructions.

atoms.canonical_statement: Preloading improved Skill-Use primarily by increasing Trigger rather than by improving execution quality after a skill was triggered.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: preloading improves SU because it raises Trigger... injection mode has little effect on execution quality after the skill is triggered.

atoms.canonical_statement: Skills with abstract names showed the largest gains from preloading, whereas keyword-rich names gained little or sometimes regressed.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Skills with abstract names... gain most, while keyword-rich names gain little or reverse.

atoms.canonical_statement: The library-scaling experiment varied the number of installed skills among 1, 10, 20, and 30 while keeping the target skill present and sampling distractors for the remaining slots.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: we install N ∈ {1, 10, 20, 30} skills into the agent’s library. The target skill is always included.

atoms.canonical_statement: The largest library-size performance drop occurred when moving from one skill to ten skills; further increases produced little additional decline.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Moving to a ten-skill library causes the visible drop... After that point, the curves change little.

atoms.canonical_statement: Most library-scaling failures were no-skill outcomes rather than selection of an incorrect distractor skill.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: most failures are runs with no skill call. Wrong-skill calls are rare.

atoms.canonical_statement: The out-of-scope evaluation contained 53 tasks that overlapped a skill topically but did not require its procedure.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We construct 53 out-of-scope tasks whose topics overlap a skill but whose requested outputs do not require that skill’s procedure.

atoms.canonical_statement: Within-scope Skill-Use and out-of-scope avoidance were negatively rank-correlated.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The rank correlation between within-scope SU and out-of-scope avoidance is negative.

atoms.canonical_statement: Over-invocation on out-of-scope tasks was driven mainly by topical overlap, especially document-shaped requests whose output did not require the skill procedure.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The over-invocations are driven by topical overlap, mostly document-shaped requests.

atoms.canonical_statement: The task-completion analysis started from 779 runs that triggered the target skill.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Under CC, we start from the 779 runs that trigger the target skill.

atoms.canonical_statement: Paired task-completion gain changed from negative to positive near a Skill-Use score of 0.5.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The paired gain turns from negative to positive near an SU score of 0.5.

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors concluded that partial or incorrect skill execution can reduce task completion below a no-skill baseline.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: A partial procedure is worse than none.

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors concluded that adding a skill library is not inherently beneficial and helps only when the agent can execute the skill procedure sufficiently well.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Adding a skill library is therefore not a free improvement; it pays off only when a model can execute the procedure.

atoms.canonical_statement: In the human audit, pairwise agreement was 86% and Cohen’s kappa was 0.65 across 100 sampled items.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: pairwise agreement is 86/100 and Cohen’s κ = 0.65.

atoms.canonical_statement: Five independent crowd annotators scored one sampled task per skill, yielding 79 audited skill-task-rubric triples.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We sample one task per skill, yielding 79 audited triples, and route them to five independent crowd annotators.

atoms.canonical_statement: The repeated-scoring robustness analysis used 83 aligned task-model observations rescored three times.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: a stratified subset of 83 aligned (task, model) observations three times

atoms.canonical_statement: Compliance had the highest repeated-score stability among the continuous metrics, with ICC(2,1) of 0.604 and within-observation standard deviation of 0.116.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Compliance 83 0.604 0.116

atoms.canonical_statement: Model rankings were unchanged for compliance weights between 0.5 and 0.75 under both harnesses.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Both harnesses give identical orderings for α ∈ [0.5, 0.75].

atoms.canonical_statement: The benchmark evaluates skill use in agentic harnesses and is not a certification of safety or deployment readiness.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The benchmark measures skill use in an agentic harness and is not a certification of safety or deployment readiness.

atoms.canonical_statement: Boundary had fewer repeated-score observations because early records omitted the field.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Boundary has fewer observations because early records omit the field.

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors stated that SKILL-USE, its construction pipeline, rubrics, and prompts would be released for reproducibility and audit.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We release SKILL-USE, together with its construction pipeline.
